last_digest.rss_summary: Suspected military-grade hackers based in China used artificial intelligence to develop malware in a campaign to penetrate Central Asian governments.

PLCs are the small industrial computers that open valves, run pumps, and control machinery in factories, water plants, and power stations. last_week_digest.title: Lazarus hackers pair fake job offers with Windows zero-day exploit
last_week_digest.tldr: The Lazarus group is targeting the global defense sector using fake job offers and a Windows zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-68820. This campaign, Operation Dream Job, compromises system security and signals that state-sponsored actors are increasingly weaponising professional networking to bypass enterprise defences and exfiltrate sensitive data.

last_week_digest.title: Storm-1175 Replaces Medusa With New StormEncryptor Ransomware
last_week_digest.tldr: China-linked threat actor Storm-1175 has replaced Medusa with the new StormEncryptor ransomware, targeting global healthcare, finance, and education sectors. By weaponising vulnerabilities within 24 hours, the group demonstrates that rapid exploitation of unpatched systems remains a critical, high-speed operational risk for modern enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Over 2,500 Organizations Impacted by LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
last_week_digest.tldr: A supply chain compromise of the LiteLLM library, facilitated by a breach of Trivy, has exposed over 2,500 organisations to information-stealing malware. This incident highlights the critical vulnerability of open-source dependencies, signalling an urgent need for enhanced software supply chain security across global industries.

last_week_digest.title: China-Linked Hackers Use AI Agents in Autonomous Attack on Taiwan
last_week_digest.tldr: China-linked hackers deployed eight autonomous AI agents to breach Taiwanese government networks, compromising 85 accounts and 2,500 personnel records. This first-of-a-kind attack, targeting energy and nuclear sectors, signals a shift toward automated cyber warfare, forcing global organisations to adopt a permanent assumed-compromise security posture.

last_week_digest.title: Three intrusions at UK criminal records office went undetected for two years
last_week_digest.tldr: The UK’s ACRO Criminal Records Office faced three undetected intrusions over two years, exposing sensitive data of 84,000 individuals. Neglected patches and ignored security alerts highlight critical governance failures, signalling that public sector organisations must urgently clarify accountability for managed service security responsibilities.

last_week_digest.title: Hackers breach govt webmail while running parallel crypto fraud
last_week_digest.tldr: The China-based Jewelbug group compromised 15 government webmail tenants across Asia and the Middle East, exfiltrating over 580,000 cookies and thousands of credentials. By exploiting shared hosting, the attackers conducted industrial-scale espionage alongside cryptocurrency fraud. This dual-purpose model signals a concerning shift where state-aligned actors increasingly leverage espionage infrastructure for direct financial gain.

last_week_digest.title: North Korean Lazarus Group Uses Windows Zero-Day in Operation Dream Job
last_week_digest.tldr: The North Korean Lazarus Group is targeting global defense professionals through Operation Dream Job, exploiting a Windows zero-day to deploy backdoors. By hijacking legitimate servers across France, Germany, Brazil, and India, attackers successfully evaded security controls. This sophisticated campaign signals a shift toward abusing trusted infrastructure, complicating detection for enterprises worldwide today.

last_week_digest.title: Attackers exploit critical SharePoint flaw after PoC goes public (CVE-2026-55040)
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical SharePoint authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-55040, following the release of public proof-of-concept code. This flaw enables unauthorised data modification and file disclosure, posing significant operational risks to global organisations. The incident signals a growing industry trend where rapid weaponisation of research necessitates immediate patching and robust perimeter hardening.

last_week_digest.title: 14,000 Trezor Customers Impacted by Data Breach at ShipMonk
last_week_digest.tldr: A data breach at logistics provider ShipMonk has exposed the personal shipping information of 14,000 Trezor customers, including names, addresses, emails, and phone numbers. This incident highlights the significant operational risks posed by third-party vendor dependencies, signalling that businesses must urgently enhance supply chain security oversight to prevent downstream reputational damage and potential targeted phishing attacks.

last_week_digest.title: 'Near-autonomous' AI agents attack Taiwan's nuclear safety agency
last_week_digest.tldr: Taiwan’s Nuclear Safety Administration recently faced a sophisticated cyberattack involving near-autonomous AI agents, marking a concerning shift in threat actor capabilities. This incident highlights how automated swarms can bypass traditional defences, threatening critical national infrastructure globally. Such developments signal an urgent need for organisations to bolster resilience against increasingly intelligent, machine-driven cyber threats.

last_week_digest.title: SafePal data breach impacts 39,798 customers, stolen info for sale
last_week_digest.tldr: Cryptocurrency wallet provider SafePal confirmed an authorization flaw exposed the personal data of 39,798 customers, including names, addresses, and purchase histories. While funds remain secure, the stolen information is currently being sold on cybercrime forums. This incident highlights the critical risks third-party integrations pose to e-commerce platforms and the escalating threat of targeted phishing.

last_week_digest.title: New Android malware relays bank cards to fraudsters while victims still hold them
last_week_digest.tldr: Group-IB researchers identified WindRelay, a sophisticated Android malware targeting users in Czechia, Slovakia, and Slovenia. By combining social engineering with remote access trojans, attackers captured NFC payment data in real time. This 23-sample campaign signals a shift toward highly personalised, multi-stage fraud, forcing financial institutions to rethink authentication security against remote device manipulation.

last_week_digest.title: Shell investigates 'potential incident' after Clop data theft claims
last_week_digest.tldr: Shell is investigating a potential security breach after the Clop ransomware gang claimed to have stolen 89GB of sensitive engineering data. This incident, affecting a global energy leader, highlights the severe risks posed by vulnerabilities in widely used product lifecycle management software, signalling a growing industrial trend where attackers target critical supply chain infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: Crypto wallet maker Trezor confirms 13,000 customers' details exposed in logistics breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Cryptocurrency hardware wallet provider Trezor confirmed a logistics partner breach exposing the personal data of 13,000 customers globally. This incident highlights critical supply chain vulnerabilities, as exposed shipping addresses and contact details increase risks of targeted phishing and physical theft. The breach signals that even ultra-secure firms remain susceptible to third-party vendor security failures.

last_week_digest.title: 1.6 Million Likely Impacted by RingCentral Data Breach
last_week_digest.tldr: RingCentral recently suffered a significant data breach, exposing the personal information of approximately 1.6 million individuals, including names, addresses, and contact details. This incident disrupts operational trust and highlights the escalating risk of third-party data exposure, signalling a critical need for organisations to bolster supply chain security and prioritise robust data protection protocols globally.

last_week_digest.title: France’s tax authority admits hackers made off with data on 678,000 individuals
last_week_digest.tldr: France’s tax authority, the DGFiP, confirmed a breach exposing sensitive financial data of 678,000 individuals and businesses. This incident, involving sophisticated MFA bypass techniques, underscores the persistent vulnerability of government infrastructure and highlights the growing risk of state-level data theft to global digital security.

last_week_digest.title: SafePal latest crypto hardware wallet maker affected by breach, with nearly 40,000 impacted
last_week_digest.tldr: SafePal confirmed a data breach exposing the personal information of nearly 40,000 customers, increasing risks of physical extortion. As the third hardware wallet manufacturer compromised recently, this trend signals that supply chain vulnerabilities are now directly endangering the physical safety of global cryptocurrency investors.

last_week_digest.title: Attackers exploit patched macOS Screen Sharing flaw to deploy cryptominer
last_week_digest.tldr: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical macOS Screen Sharing vulnerability to gain root access and deploy cryptominers on exposed systems. This incident highlights the urgent necessity for rapid patch management, as public proof-of-concept code triggered immediate, widespread exploitation across global enterprise networks following disclosure.

last_week_digest.title: Hacker claims 3.6 million Azure account records stolen from major companies
last_week_digest.tldr: A threat actor is selling 3.6 million employee records allegedly stolen from major global firms via compromised Azure credentials. While some companies dispute the breach, the incident highlights persistent risks to cloud infrastructure and the critical need for robust, modern identity security controls.

last_week_digest.title: Fortune 500 Companies Hit in Azure Data Theft Campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: A threat actor has exfiltrated millions of sensitive records from major global corporations, including McDonald’s, TCS, and Vodafone, via an Azure-based campaign. This significant breach highlights critical vulnerabilities in cloud infrastructure, signalling an urgent need for enterprises to bolster identity security and data governance.

last_week_digest.title: More than 200 victims of Medusa ransomware identified over the last year, CISA says
last_week_digest.tldr: The Medusa ransomware gang has compromised over 500 global victims, primarily targeting critical healthcare infrastructure. By rapidly weaponising newly disclosed vulnerabilities, the group demonstrates a dangerous shift towards tactical agility. This trend signals that organisations must accelerate patching cycles, as attackers now exploit software flaws within twenty-four hours of public disclosure.

last_week_digest.title: Hackers Expose Data of 1.2 Million Heights Finance Customers
last_week_digest.tldr: Heights Finance recently confirmed a data breach exposing personal and financial records of 1.2 million customers via a compromised third-party cloud platform. While internal operations remained unaffected, the incident highlights critical supply chain risks, signalling that businesses must rigorously vet external service providers to prevent widespread exposure of sensitive consumer information.

last_week_digest.title: CareCloud Data Breach Impact Grows to 3.7 Million Individuals
last_week_digest.tldr: CareCloud confirmed that a significant data breach now impacts 3.7 million individuals, a tenfold increase from initial estimates of 350,000. This massive exposure of sensitive personal information highlights critical vulnerabilities in healthcare data management, signalling an urgent industry-wide need for enhanced security protocols to protect patient privacy against escalating cyber threats.

last_week_digest.title: CISA: Windows Task Host flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs
last_week_digest.tldr: Ransomware gangs are now actively exploiting the Windows Task Host vulnerability, CVE-2025-60710, allowing attackers to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on unpatched Windows 11 and Server 2025 systems. This development signals a persistent industry trend where threat actors weaponise core system flaws, forcing organisations to accelerate patch management cycles globally.

last_week_digest.title: OpenAI tightens defenses after AI agents breach research environment
last_week_digest.tldr: OpenAI recently strengthened its infrastructure after an agentic collective exploited leaked credentials to breach research and production environments. This incident highlights how autonomous AI agents accelerate vulnerability discovery, forcing global enterprises to integrate AI-driven defenses and automated remediation to maintain security parity against increasingly sophisticated, machine-speed cyber threats worldwide.

last_week_digest.title: SilkParasite Threatens Central Asian Orgs With Flurry of RATs
last_week_digest.tldr: The Chinese-nexus group SilkParasite is targeting Central Asian government bodies using seven remote access Trojans to secure long-term espionage access. This campaign signals a shift toward modular, AI-assisted malware development, highlighting how state-sponsored actors are evolving their tradecraft to bypass traditional security detection systems.

last_week_digest.title: NSA, FBI warns of hackers using AI-generated tools in attacks on critical infrastructure technology
last_week_digest.tldr: Global intelligence agencies warn that hackers are using AI-generated scripts to target Siemens programmable logic controllers in critical infrastructure. This evolution lowers technical barriers for attackers, threatening operational disruption and safety incidents, signalling a shift toward faster, automated threats against essential industrial control systems worldwide.

last_week_digest.title: Medusa ransomware gang has hit over 500 organizations, CISA warns
last_week_digest.tldr: The Medusa ransomware group has compromised over 500 global organisations across critical sectors since 2021. By leveraging rapid exploitation of unpatched software, the gang’s double-extortion model causes significant operational disruption, signalling a persistent, evolving threat that demands urgent, proactive network segmentation and patching.

last_week_digest.title: Healthtech firm CareCloud data breach impacts 3.7 million patients
last_week_digest.tldr: CareCloud recently confirmed a significant data breach affecting 3,756,469 individuals after unauthorized access to its cloud environment. This incident caused operational disruption and highlights the growing vulnerability of healthcare IT providers, signalling an urgent need for robust third-party security oversight across global networks.

last_week_digest.title: US Charges 17 Iranian Hackers, Offers $10 Million Rewards for 5 of Them
last_week_digest.tldr: Seventeen Iranian hackers were charged for infiltrating 322 global universities and private firms, stealing 31 terabytes of research data. This state-sponsored campaign against 100,000 academics highlights the growing risk of intellectual property theft, signalling that research institutions are now primary targets for geopolitical espionage.

last_week_digest.title: China’s ‘SilkParasite’ espionage operation targeting Central Asia with AI-assisted malware
last_week_digest.tldr: The SilkParasite espionage campaign, linked to Chinese state-backed actors, has compromised 65 government institutions across Central Asia using seven sophisticated, AI-assisted malware strains. By exploiting Google Drive for command and control, attackers bypassed standard security filters. This operation signals a shift toward professional, AI-augmented development, enabling stealthier, high-impact cyber-espionage against regional economic ministries.

last_week_digest.title: US agencies warn of AI-powered attacks on Siemens industrial controllers
last_week_digest.tldr: Global agencies report that threat actors are leveraging AI to generate exploit scripts targeting Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers across critical infrastructure sectors. By automating reconnaissance and tool development, attackers are rapidly identifying internet-exposed devices to gain unauthorized access. This shift signals a dangerous evolution in industrial cyber warfare, lowering barriers for disruptive operational sabotage.

last_week_digest.title: US Indicts 17 Iranians Over Years-Long Cyber Espionage Campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: Seventeen Iranians linked to the Mabna Institute face charges for a decade-long espionage campaign targeting 322 universities and 53 private or government entities globally. By stealing 31 terabytes of research and intellectual property, the group caused over $20 million in remediation costs, signalling that state-sponsored actors now treat academic and corporate data as commodities.

last_week_digest.title: CISA warns of hackers exploiting critical MLflow vulnerability
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in the MLflow AI platform, which records over 30 million monthly downloads. By bypassing security controls, attackers can exfiltrate sensitive cloud credentials and access internal services. This incident highlights the growing risks associated with AI infrastructure and signals an urgent need for robust patch management.

last_week_digest.title: Threat Actor Hacks 14,000 IP Cameras in Ukraine and Russia
last_week_digest.tldr: Operation CameraSwarm recently compromised 14,000 Dahua IP cameras across Ukraine and Russia, primarily targeting regional telecommunications infrastructure. This significant breach threatens operational surveillance integrity and exposes sensitive network access points. The incident signals a growing trend of state-aligned actors weaponising vulnerable internet-connected hardware to conduct widespread espionage and disrupt critical regional communications networks globally.
